summary: Stub package pulls install-scripted tarball from non-registry third-party host
details: merchantweb-lang-cookie-reset@0.0.6 ships a 3-line index.js that only exports {name, version} and declares a single dependency resolved from a URL outside the npm registry: "packet-table-thread-stream": "https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/packet-table-thread-stream". The shrinkwrap records hasInstallScript: true for that dependency, so on npm install the tarball is fetched from artifacts.yosiroute.com and its lifecycle scripts are executed on the installer's machine. Package metadata is placeholder — author "Package Registry" and a repository URL pointing at github.com/example/... unrelated to the artifact host — and the module itself provides no functionality, so its only install-time effect is to pull attacker-controllable, install-scripted code from a mutable third-party endpoint into the dependency tree.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
